neighbours.label: the start of a qualifier that restricts a statement to particular circumstances ('when we …', 'at pressure above …', 'on a given …', 'in patients with …'); the output direction promotes 'depending', 'specific', 'certain', 'particular'
fire: My daughter gets carsick when we drive on winding roads for more than an hour.
The alloy becomes brittle at temperatures below minus forty degrees.
The drug causes a rash in patients with a particular genetic variant.
The algorithm finds the shortest path on a given graph of cities and roads.
You save the most money when you use the card at participating stores.
Water boils at a lower temperature at altitudes above three thousand metres.
The rule applies only to drivers under a certain age in a given state.
The dog barks loudly when we leave the house without him.
quiet: My daughter was carsick yesterday and slept through the whole afternoon.
The alloy is brittle and cracked along its entire length.
The drug caused a rash and the doctor stopped the treatment.
The algorithm is fast and found the shortest path between the two cities.
You saved a lot of money and bought a new bicycle.
Water boiled in the kettle and steam filled the small kitchen.
The rule is old and most drivers have forgotten it.
The dog barked loudly and the neighbours complained again.

notes: Low-max pole (17.9) with mixed prose and code examples; probes of qualifier sentences 0.14-0.50.
